title: Exact Analytical Treatment of Collectively Pumped Dicke Superradiance
authors: Avishi Poddar, Nico Baßler, Julian Lyne, Susanne F. Yelin, Helmut Ritsch, Claudiu Genes, Raphael Holzinger
abstract: We study the dynamics of an ensemble of $N$ two-level emitters undergoing collective decay at rate $Γ$ and collective incoherent pumping at rate $R$, confined to the fully symmetric Dicke ladder. Although the population dynamics are confined to a finite set of rate equations, their quantum-trajectory representation involves infinitely many pump-decay histories. We derive an exact finite continued fraction for the Laplace-transformed Dicke-state populations by resumming the infinitely many quantum trajectories generated by competing pump and decay processes. Our construction provides a physically transparent interpretation of the tridiagonal resolvent and extends to arbitrary permutationally symmetric initial states. In the strong- and weak-pumping regimes, we obtain perturbative transient solutions. We also identify exact relaxation eigenvalues and emission observables at balanced pump and decay strengths. Our solution provides a starting point for extending trajectory-based analytical methods to more general driven-dissipative collective systems.
summary: This paper provides an exact analytical solution for the dynamics of Dicke superradiance using a novel technique based on quantum trajectories. By resumming infinite jump histories into a finite continued fraction, the authors determine the time evolution of the emitter populations. This method offers a powerful tool for analyzing complex driven-dissipative quantum systems beyond simple rate equations.
main_problem: The paper analytically solves the time evolution of an ensemble of N two-level emitters undergoing collective decay and incoherent pumping.
main_result: The exact dynamics are derived by constructing a finite continued fraction representation for the Laplace-transformed state populations, providing an analytical solution across various pumping regimes.
method: The core method involves using quantum trajectory theory to resum infinitely many pump-decay histories into a closed-form, finite continued fraction structure in Laplace space.
model_or_system: The system is Dicke superradiance, modeled by N two-level emitters coupled symmetrically, whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation restricted to the fully symmetric Dicke ladder.
key_observables: Dicke-state populations, collective emission rate (Iss), and the zero-delay second-order correlation function g(2)(0).
important_parameters: The pumping rate (R), decay rate (Γ), and the number of emitters (N); the analysis focuses on the balanced point (R=Γ).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes permutationally symmetric initial states, confining the dynamics to the fully symmetric Dicke subspace.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Dicke ladder decomposition, while Figure 2 schematically shows the quantum-trajectory resummation forming the continued fraction.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the rate equations, derives the Laplace transform representation, and then develops the key result: the exact finite continued fraction by summing over quantum jump histories, followed by regime analyses (weak/strong pumping) and calculation of observables.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, exact analytical technique (continued fractions from quantum trajectories) for solving driven-dissipative quantum systems, which is highly relevant for open quantum systems research in cavity QED and quantum optics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Collectively pumped Dicke superradiance. (a) The Hilbert space of N spin-1/2 emitters decomposes into Dicke ladders |J, M⟩of fixed total angular momentum J. Ver- tical transitions M →M ± 1 preserve J, so that each J ladder forms an invariant dynamical subspace, remains de- coupled from all other ladders, and contains 2J + 1 states. (b) In the fully symmetric ladder J = N/2, the dynamics are restricted to the N + 1 Dicke states |m⟩, labeled by m = M + N/2 = 0, . . . , N. Collective pumping ( ˆJ†) and collective dissipation ( ˆJ) induce upward and downward transi- tions, respectively.

FIG. 2. Quantum-trajectory resummation. Schematic representation of the exact trajectory construction for the Laplace- transformed population Pk(s), starting from the Dicke ground state |0⟩. The direct upward trajectory |0⟩→|1⟩→· · · →|k⟩ contributes ePk(s) [Eq. (18)]. All additional trajectories are generated by inserting closed pump–decay excursions, which are resummed by the continued-fraction factors Fm(s) [Eq. (19)]. Each factor Fm(s) accounts for excursions from |m −1⟩to |m⟩ and back, including nested excursions to higher Dicke states. In particular, Fk+1(s) accounts for excursions above the final state |k⟩. Their product yields the exact population Pk(s) [Eq. (17)].
